title: Rust binding proposals need runtime source and result integrity
wanted_capability: Apply Rust binding proposals through edits.* without changing literal data, losing field attributes, synthesizing getter calls for field reads, duplicating new-file changes, or overstating trait object safety.
missing_primitive: Runtime and compiler validated Rust binding proposal contracts
fallback_used: Isolated multi-module fixtures, exact edits.* application, compiled runtime assertions, and explicit compiler-guided caller repair.
notes: Live installed-isolate probes reproduced data-literal rewrites, cfg-field attribute loss, impossible getter calls, duplicate create/edit targets, and false dyn compatibility. Source repairs are being validated through a rebuilt native isolate. No operator acknowledgement grants were supplied.
resolution_note: Repaired literal/comment protection, create/edit separation, field attributes and access syntax, trait extraction and object-safety reports, diagnostic anchoring disclosure, bounded caller rewriting, and default extraction visibility. All 21 executable Rust cases pass through rebuilt isolate across 15 bindings, with edits application and rustc/runtime evidence. Baseline has 8 pass/13 fail. Evidence: scripts/audit-rust-bindings-runtime.py and design/bro-harness/model-facing-audit/rust-runtime-{audit.md,baseline.json,verified.json}. Operator authority refusals remain intact; no acknowledge_* grants invented.
